sections.h2: Where is Somerville, and why does density matter for property tax?
sections.html:
Somerville is a city directly northwest of Boston and north of Cambridge, in Middlesex County. It covers about 4.2 square miles, of which roughly 4.1 are land, and it borders Cambridge, Medford, Everett, Arlington and the Charlestown neighborhood of Boston.

The 2020 census counted 81,045 residents. Wikipedia reports that this makes Somerville the most densely populated municipality in New England and the 19th most densely populated incorporated place in the country.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Somerville's squares and hills?
sections.html:
Somerville's geography was shaped by glaciers, and its neighborhoods grew around commercial squares. Ridges left by glaciation became known as the Seven Hills of Somerville: Central Hill, Clarendon Hill, Cobble Hill, Ploughed Hill, Prospect Hill, Spring Hill and Winter Hill. The Mystic River runs along the north, Alewife Brook along the west and the Millers River along the southeast.

The city was set off from Charlestown as a town in 1842 and became a city in 1872. The Middlesex Canal passed through in 1803, and the Fitchburg Railroad reached the area in 1841, followed by passenger service in 1843. Industry, then housing, followed the rails.

  • Union Square and Davis Square were the largest commercial areas through the early 20th century.
  • Ball Square, Magoun Square, Teele Square and Gilman Square grew as smaller centers.
  • The Red Line Northwest Extension reached Davis Square in 1984.

Ask the Assessing Department how your parcel is classified and valued, since the squares differ in character.

In 2016, Mass General Brigham moved its headquarters to Assembly Square, and other corporate offices have followed at Assembly Row and Union Square. Tufts University's campus runs along the Somerville and Medford line, so its Tisch Library straddles the boundary. Somerville Public Schools enrolled 4,876 students in the 2025 to 2026 school year across ten schools.

sections.h2: Which offices handle Somerville property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work. The Assessing Department sets values, keeps ownership and mailing records, and decides abatements. The Treasurer/Collector bills and collects the tax.

  • Assessing: email assessing@somervillema.gov or call 617-625-6600, extension 3100.
  • Treasury: 93 Highland Avenue, Somerville, MA 02143, email treasury@somervillema.gov, phone 617-625-6600, extension 3500. The treasurer listed on the city page is Linda Dubuque.
  • Office hours listed for Treasury: Monday to Wednesday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Thursday 8:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., Friday 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.

The city warns that Doxo is not affiliated with Somerville for online bill payment, and it directs residents to somervillema.gov/Payments instead.

sections.h2: When are Somerville property taxes due?
sections.html:
Somerville bills quarterly, and taxes are due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. If a date falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day. The fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30.

QuarterCoversDueType of bill
1July 1 to Sept. 30Aug. 1Preliminary (estimated)
2Oct. 1 to Dec. 31Nov. 1Preliminary (estimated)
3Jan. 1 to March 31Feb. 1Actual
4April 1 to June 30May 1Actual

The preliminary bills are based on the previous year's actual tax. The city's formula adds 2.5% to last year's actual tax and divides the result by four. In December the assessors set the real tax for the year, and the two preliminary payments are subtracted from it. Bills go out one month before the due date.

Ask the Assessing Department for the rate on your classification.

sections.h2: What happens if a Somerville tax bill is paid late?
sections.html:
Late bills accrue interest, and Somerville does not accept postmarks as proof of payment. A bill counts as paid only when the Treasurer receives it.

  • Real estate, personal property and water balances carry 14% interest under M.G.L. c. 59, sections 57 and 57C, according to the city's FAQ.
  • Once a tax is taken, tax title interest is 16% under M.G.L. c. 60, section 62.
  • A returned check costs $25, and 1% applies if it exceeds $2,500.
  • An $18 demand fee is added to a fourth quarter bill that is not paid on time.
  • Unpaid water, sewer or ticket liens are added to the third quarter bill.

The city also says that failing to receive a bill does not excuse payment. A bill is generated for every parcel, and the owner must ask for a duplicate if needed. The Treasurer/Collector's page also links delinquent real estate information and a tax title report.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Somerville assessment?
sections.html:
File an abatement application with the Assessors by February 1, 2027 at 4:30 p.m. The city's page states that applications must be received in the Assessors' Office by the close of business on February 1, or the Board of Assessors loses jurisdiction to abate the bill.

  1. Get the application at the Assessor's Office or download it from the city's abatement page.
  2. Submit it by hand, by mail with a postmark of February 1 or earlier, or by fax or email to assessing@somervillema.gov so long as it arrives by close of business that day.
  3. The Board of Assessors has three months from the application date to decide.
  4. If you disagree, appeal to the state Appellate Tax Board within three months of the Board's notice.

Filing does not stop collection. Pay on time to avoid interest and to preserve your appeal rights.

sections.h2: What happens to Somerville property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Taxes follow the owner of record on January 1 for the fiscal year, so a bill can reach you after you sell. The city's FAQ explains that by operation of law the January 1 owner's name appears on the next fiscal year's four bills, and the buyer can ask Assessing to add a c/o line with the new name. Check at closing that neither your mortgage company nor your attorney pays the same installment twice.

Refunds work the same way. Credits on real estate or personal property bills are refunded at the end of the fiscal year to the January 1 record owner, and credits do not roll into the next year. If a property transfers during the year, the city says such matters should be handled at closing.

  • Order a municipal lien certificate. The city lists fees of $80 for a single family, condo, two family or three family, $250 for four to eight units, and $350 for an apartment building of more than eight units.
  • Get a final water reading from the Water Department and give it to closing counsel so any credit is received at closing. If a water credit comes from overestimated bills and will not be used within the next billing cycle, send a written refund request to the Water and Sewer department at 17 Franey Road.
  • If you own a condominium in a newly developed building, the master parcel may still carry one tax bill, and the association is responsible for keeping that account at zero at each due date.

sections.h2: Can I sell my Somerville house if I owe tax?
sections.html:
Yes. A sale with tax due is routine: the lien certificate shows what is owed, and the balance is paid from sale proceeds at closing. A cash buyer can purchase the house as is, even with the bill outstanding, and the title company settles the amount before funds go to you.

If a bill stays unpaid, the city can take the tax and publish a notice of tax taking, and the balance then carries the 16% tax title rate. That is one reason to act before it happens. Call or text us with your address and the amount you believe you owe, and we will tell you what we can offer, with no obligation.

faqs.q: When are Somerville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. The fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30, and bills go out one month before each due date.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to file a Somerville abatement?
faqs.a: The deadline stated on the city's page is February 1, 2027 at 4:30 p.m. Applications mailed with a postmark of February 1 or earlier are accepted, and fax or email is accepted if it is received by close of business.

faqs.q: Does Somerville accept postmarks for tax payments?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer says bills are paid only when received, and a postmark on an envelope is not accepted as the payment date.

faqs.q: What interest does Somerville charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: The city's FAQ lists 14% on late real estate, personal property and water balances, and 16% once a tax is taken and moved to tax title.

faqs.q: I sold my house, but I still got a tax bill. What should I do?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner's name stays on the bill for that fiscal year. Confirm your attorney handled the proration, then send the bill to the new owner, who can ask Assessing to add a c/o line.

faqs.q: How much is a Somerville municipal lien certificate?
faqs.a: The city lists $80 for single, two and three family homes and condos, $250 for four to eight units and $350 for larger apartment buildings. Confirm the fee with the Treasury office before ordering.
